Sitting around the table were my parents, sisters and brother-in-law, all of us immigrants who came to Australia from Fiji. My niece and her siblings were born in Australia. item.title: Review: Even Hawaiʻi’s most Republican island can’t escape the blue wave
item.description: During the midterm elections, Ni‘ihau backed Democrats for their governors, casting 14 of their 21 votes for Josh Green and Derek Kawakami The secluded island of Ni‘ihau has long been a Republican stronghold in deep blue Hawai‘i. Ni‘ihauans have an unusual tendency to unanimously support conservative candidates, like in 2020, when all 43 Ni‘ihauan voters cast their ballots for Donald Trump. This has been the case since as far back as the early 1900s, when Ni‘ihau’s ballots were sometimes relayed to the neighboring island of Kaua‘i via carrier pigeon.
